name: Sufentanil
summary: An synthetic analgesic drug that is roughly between 5-10x the potency of it's parent drug, (Fentanyl); It's use is very contained to surgery and post-operative pain.
metabolism: Evidence is from Dzuveo 30 microgram sublingual tablets. Biotransformation takes place primarily in the liver and the small intestine. Sufentanil is mainly metabolised in humans by the cytochrome P450 3A4 enzyme system, and is rapidly metabolised to a number of inactive metabolites, with oxidative N- and O-dealkylation being the major routes of elimination. The sublingual route gives a mean absolute bioavailability of 53% relative to a one-minute intravenous infusion of the same dose, because it avoids intestinal and first-pass hepatic 3A4 metabolism, compared with 9% for swallowed oral administration. The central volume of distribution after intravenous application is about 14 litres and the steady-state volume of distribution about 350 litres. After a single administration of Dzuveo the mean terminal phase half-life was 13.4 hours (range 2.5-34.4 hours).
